title: Find Weighted Median Node in Tree
summary: Given an integer n and an undirected, weighted tree rooted at node 0 with n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1, represented by a 2D array edges, and a 2D integer array queries, for each query determine the first node x on the path from uj to vj where the sum of edge weights from uj to x is at least half of the total path weight.
statement: Given an integer n and an undirected, weighted tree rooted at node 0 with n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1, represented by a 2D array edges, and a 2D integer array queries, for each query determine the first node x on the path from uj to vj where the sum of edge weights from uj to x is at least half of the total path weight. Return an array ans where ans[j] is the node index of the weighted median for each query.
constraints: The positive-weight tree has up to 100,000 nodes rooted at zero.
For each ordered pair u,v, walk from u toward v.
Return the first node whose accumulated weight is at least half the total path weight.
hints: The answer lies either on the upward u-to-LCA segment or the downward LCA-to-v segment, selected by weighted distance.
Preprocess root distances and ancestors, then binary-lift to the boundary immediately before or at the half-weight threshold.
Find LCA and total weight; on the u side jump while still below half, otherwise lift from v to the highest descendant already at or beyond half.
Positive weights make accumulated path weight strictly increasing, so binary lifting locates the unique first threshold-crossing node.
editorial: Positive weights make accumulated path weight strictly increasing, so binary lifting locates the unique first threshold-crossing node.

tests.explanation: The sole edge crosses halfway in either direction, so each answer is the destination.
Both weighted paths first cross their halfway point at node two.
